subject: MAP: risk-adjusted token economics & evaluation plan — assumptions review
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Miller <sara@celestahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: risk-adjusted token economics & evaluation plan — assumptions review

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the productive demo yesterday. As promised, I pulled together a short mutual action plan (MAP) focus for the evaluation/close that prioritizes the unit economics checks we discussed (tokens/$, caching, and batching). I attached a concise assumptions workbook for your review.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm expected average request size (tokens in prompt + expected completion) for the pilot endpoints (sample payloads appreciated).
- Confirm expected traffic shape (steady vs burst & concurrency peaks) so we can validate batching behavior.
- Share procurement timeline / PO owner so Ben can coordinate pricing/terms.

High-level assumptions in the attached:
- Avg tokens per API call: 420 (prompt 320 + completion 100) — adjustable with your sample data.
- Caching hit rate (prefix/KV-style): baseline 25% — can improve to 40% with deterministic prefixing.
- Preferred batching target: 6–8 requests per batch for a p95 latency goal of ~250ms on our Dedicated tier.
- Fallback plan: quantized 8-bit variant for daytime spikes to control cost; higher-quality 16-bit for critical flows.

Proposed MAP timeline (placeholder):
- Thu Apr 8: technical deep-dive (30m) — Neha to lead.
- Wed Apr 14: finalize MAP and acceptance criteria.
- Wed Apr 28: procurement & PO.
- Mon May 10: pilot go-live.

If you want, Neha can run a quick token-profile with a 1-hour session using a small sample of your traffic to validate the token assumptions and show the cost delta with/without caching.

Attachments: MAP_assumptions_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —

Hi Jordan —

Thanks, this looks helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we lock the MAP: 

1) The 420 tokens/call — is that an average across both user chat and automated summarization flows? Our summarize flow tends to be narrower (prompt ~150, completion ~40) but our diagnostic chat can be much larger.

2) For caching: will prefix caching work for any free-text queries, or only for templated requests? We do have some templated forms but a fair amount of free text as well.

3) We’ll likely have a daily burst when patients get appointment reminders (concurrent spikes). How does batching behave under bursts vs sustained traffic?

Attaching a small traffic extract (redacted) so you can see sample payload sizes.

—Sara
Sara Miller
Head of Integrations | Celesta Health
sara@celestahealth.com
Attachment: celesta_traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Miller <sara@celestahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: risk-adjusted token economics & evaluation plan — assumptions review

Hi Sara —

Good questions — I pulled a quick technical note based on the sample you shared. TL;DR: prefix caching helps the templated flows the most; for free-text we can still get benefit from partial KV caching and answer-level caching on stable prompts. Here are the working assumptions I recommend we lock in for the MAP so cost modeling is aligned: 

Assumptions (provisional, adjustable after the tech session):
- Token profile: median 310 tokens/call, 75th pct 620 tokens/call (your CSV shows mixture of short summarization + long chat). I recommend we run a 1-hour token-profile job to produce exact percentiles.
- Cache model:
  - Templated prefix hit-rate (pilot): 35%
  - Free-text partial/KV hit-rate (pilot): 12%
  - Combined effective hit-rate: 24%
- Batching & latency:
  - Target batch size: 8 (configurable).
  - Expected p95 latency with batching (Dedicated, 8 GPUs equiv): ~220–300ms depending on token distribution.
  - During bursts, batching becomes less efficient (shorter queues) but we can enable a small temporary scale-up/burst policy to preserve latency SLOs.
- Cost sensitivity:
  - With 24% effective caching and batching=8, expected tokens per billed call reduces by ~18% vs no-cache/no-batch baseline.
  - Quantization (8-bit) on non-critical routes can reduce compute cost by ~25% with small quality degradation; keep a 16-bit route for safety.

Next steps I propose:
1) 30-minute technical session — Thu Apr 8 at 10:00 PT (I’ll run a live token profile from your CSV and show the workbook).
2) Post-session: I’ll update MAP_assumptions_v1.xlsx with measured percentiles and re-run the cost sheet (tokens/$ delta scenarios).
3) Jordan/Ben: share procurement owner and desired billing model (monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go) so we can align the price ladder.

Attachment: MAP_assumptions_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Happy to adjust — pick a time if the Thu slot doesn’t work.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
